messages:
anya: Heads up — after merge 9f2c1a we saw a ~20% p50 latency increase on long-seq runs. I attached an nsys capture and a perfetto snippet. Timeline points to extra host<->device memcpy around the selector/handoff path. Anyone have cycles to eyeball traces?

sam k: I noticed the same in nightly. nvtx shows more small memcpys clustered during kernel selection. Not a single big memcpy but many little ones.

li chen: Re-ran locally with nsys and filtered to cuda,osrt. command I used: `nsys profile -o /tmp/trace -t cuda,osrt ./runner --workload long-seq`

li chen: short excerpt from the timeline:
```
kernel_selector      12.3ms -> 29.1ms
pack_inputs          3.8ms  -> 12.6ms
cudaMemcpyAsync H2D  8.7ms  -> 19.4ms (many short transfers)
runner_dispatch      1.2ms  -> 4.9ms
```

mike r: that aligns with the change I merged — async-batcher now prefetches per-request to try to reduce tail latency. commit 9f2c1a added per-request prefetch which may be causing extra pinned->device ops.

tracebot: bisect result: first bad commit: 9f2c1a (reproducer run 2026-03-14T08:12:00Z) — confidence high

anya: thanks. can someone run the selector with NVTX spans so we can see CPU vs GPU splits? I want to know if the selector is blocking on host packing or if memcopies are serialized.

sam k: added NVTX around select_start/select_end in a quick patch. command to profile: `nsys profile -o /tmp/annot -t cuda,osrt --trace-cuda-memory true ./runner`

sam k: NVTX shows selector CPU prepare_keys ~6ms, then pack_inputs (copies) 14ms, then several tiny kernel launches. There is a visible hopback between host work and device memcpy which seems to cause stalls.

li chen: hypothesis: prefetch path uses non-pinned buffers then does cudaMemcpyAsync which stalls until pinned staging happens. If prefetch does many small transfers instead of coalesced pinned batch transfer, that explains the extra overhead.

mike r: quick experiment — toggled PREFETCH_BATCH=0 to disable prefetch and re-ran. p50 reverted close to baseline in staging perf. Not definitive but points at prefetch logic.

anya: can you paste the quick perf numbers?

mike r: baseline p50 18.6ms, with 9f2c1a and default prefetch p50 22.5ms, with PREFETCH_BATCH=0 p50 18.9ms.

li chen: I also instrumented with cudaMemcpyKind logging. saw ~40 extra H2D memcpy calls per second in the problematic run vs baseline. Most are small (<8KB).

sam k: suggested mitigation: switch prefetch to use a pinned staging buffer pool and coalesce multiple small keys into one larger transfer. Quick pseudo:
```
// use pinned pool
void *p = pinned_pool.alloc(total_bytes);
memcpy(p, keys_blob, total_bytes);
cudaMemcpyAsync(devbuf, p, total_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, stream);
```

anya: good plan. additional check: make sure pack_inputs doesn't call any sync API (cudaStreamSynchronize or implicit sync). Also check memcpy direction flags.

mike r: I'll prototype pinned pool and run nsys. If that removes the hopback we can roll as hotfix.

li chen: I'll open a PR with the profiling artifacts and a microbenchmark that shows the small-transfer penalty. tagging perf/regression and eng-runtime.

tracebot: PR created: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2345 with label perf/regression

deploy-bot: staged branch perf/eviction-staging deployed to perf env (small run queued)

anya: awesome. next steps — mike, plumb pinned pool and run nsys with the same filters, then re-run bisect to confirm 9f2c1a is the root cause. If pinned pool removes the extra memcpys we can either revert prefetch or change its implementation. :thumbsup:

sam k: also adding a one-line NVTX wrapper in the selector so future traces show the exact boundary — saves a lot of guesswork.

li chen: attaching the nsys filenames in the PR for posterity. we should add a perf test in CI that checks p50 for long-seq after any changes to the batcher/prefetch path.

mike r: thanks all, will follow up with traces and numbers shortly.
